limitations: The representative finding does not provide the exact imported Joda-Time classes, resolved call signature, dependency version, or build configuration.
Call-shaped source text is weaker evidence than semantic symbol resolution.
The detector message does not prove that a Joda-Time API member is annotated with Java's @Deprecated annotation.
The detector does not prove a vulnerability, exploit path, reachable execution, shipped artifact, or failed compatibility migration.
predicates: A source reference or call resolves to a class from the joda-time artifact, ordinarily in the org.joda.time namespace.
The source location belongs to the analyzer's selected scope and build variant.
The rule's library-classification metadata maps the resolved library/API use to the Joda-Time migration concern.
detector_semantics.claim: A Joda-Time library/API use is detected in analyzed source and classified as a deprecated-library migration concern; the reported message identifies java.time, including Android desugared support where applicable, as the intended replacement family.

unknowns: Which exact Joda-Time class, constructor, factory, and method call caused the representative finding.
Which joda-time version and dependency path are resolved for the analyzed artifact.
Whether the referenced source is compiled and packaged for production.
Whether the finding concerns direct code use, a transitive dependency, or generated source.
Whether a concrete security advisory applies to the resolved version.
Whether the target Android deployment requires desugaring and, if so, whether every needed java.time API is supported.
Whether java.time substitution is behaviorally equivalent for the actual patterns, chronology, locale, and time-zone semantics.

documented_behavior: Joda-Time publishes org.joda.time as its Java module and documents DateTime plus a formatter/parser API.
org.joda.time.format.DateTimeFormatter formats and parses Joda-Time values; documented parsing behavior can involve chronology, formatter override settings, and default time-zone behavior.

java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter creates pattern-based formatters and formats TemporalAccessor instances. Its pattern language, resolver behavior, locale handling, and zone requirements must be evaluated independently from Joda-Time behavior.
Android documents that a subset of java.time is available through core-library desugaring and publishes a per-API support table.
preconditions: For a Joda-Time formatter call, the formatter factory/result and target value must resolve to the documented Joda-Time types.
For java.time formatting, the supplied TemporalAccessor must provide fields required by the formatter; formatting can throw DateTimeException.
For Android use below native platform availability, the exact java.time APIs used must be supported by the configured core-library-desugaring version and selected build variant.
unknowns: The exact Joda-Time formatter, pattern, locale, chronology, time zone, parse mode, and source/target temporal types used by the reported code are not provided.
Whether the analyzed Android build enables core-library desugaring is not provided.
Whether a candidate java.time formatter API is supported by the actual Android Gradle Plugin and desugared-library versions is not provided.

events.condition: Observation: source contains a Joda-Time import or type reference. Predicate: symbol resolution must confirm binding to the joda-time artifact rather than text in a comment or string, or a same-named local type.
events.name: joda_time_type_reference_observed

events.condition: Observation: a formatter-factory call is present. Predicate: the receiver must resolve to org.joda.time.format.DateTimeFormat and the resulting value or invocation must be part of compiled source for the analyzed variant.
events.name: joda_time_formatter_factory_call_observed

events.condition: Observation: formatting/parsing-like syntax is present near a Joda-Time formatter reference. Predicate: method resolution must establish that the invoked member belongs to org.joda.time.format.DateTimeFormatter; the textual substrings alone do not establish this.
events.name: joda_time_format_or_parse_use_observed

important_note: DeprecatedLibrarySpec is a detector concern label, not an API class, protocol, CrySL rule, or governed type named DeprecatedLibrarySpec. The consulted Joda-Time maintainer source describes the project as largely finished, with no major enhancements planned, and directs Java SE 8 users toward java.time. This does not establish that every Joda-Time API is annotated @Deprecated, that every installed version is vulnerable, or that a particular finding is exploitable. The representative finding provides a Joda-Time library message but not its resolved AST call target; the listed types are limited to documented Joda-Time date-formatting types consistent with the reported formatting context.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That a type, API, framework specification, or CrySL rule named DeprecatedLibrarySpec exists.
That the reported application method calls any particular Joda-Time member beyond what resolved source or bytecode proves.
That every org.joda.time type or method is itself annotated @Deprecated.
That the dependency is unmaintained, end-of-life, vulnerable, or absent from vendor support merely because the detector emits this migration message.
That a known CVE affects the resolved joda-time version.
That java.time replacement APIs are available on every Android device configuration without checking minSdkVersion, Android Gradle Plugin configuration, and the exact desugared API table.
That migration preserves parser behavior, chronology, locale, time-zone, default-zone, resolver, or formatting-pattern semantics.
That the finding reaches production code rather than test, debug-only, generated, dead, compile-only, or excluded source.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: Executing Joda-Time formatting or parsing does not by itself demonstrate a vulnerability or a CWE-1104 condition. A runtime security claim requires evidence about the shipped dependency version, maintenance/support status relevant to that version, exposure, and an applicable vulnerability or security consequence.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The detector identifies use of a library whose maintainers describe it as largely finished and direct Java SE 8 users toward java.time.

compatibility: Exact Joda-Time parsing/formatting patterns, locale, chronology, default-zone, explicit-zone, and error-handling behavior.
Exact target java.time types and formatter APIs.
Android minSdkVersion, Android Gradle Plugin version, core-library-desugaring configuration, desugar_jdk_libs version, and confirmation in the official desugared API support table.
Behavioral comparison covering time zones, daylight-saving transitions, locale output, invalid input, partial temporal values, and parser resolution.
runtime: Artifact/package evidence that the resolved joda-time dependency is shipped in the relevant runtime artifact.
Reachability evidence that the identified code path executes in the relevant deployment.
If asserting a security issue, an applicable advisory/CVE, affected version range, and exposure path.
source_level: Resolved import, type, constructor, factory, or method-call evidence binding the finding to the joda-time artifact.
Resolved dependency coordinates and version for the analyzed build variant.
Exact source scope classification: production, test, debug, generated, compile-only, or excluded.

name: DeprecatedLibrarySpec
semantic_scope: For every finding of this rule, the detector observes source-level use of the Joda-Time library or a resolved Joda-Time API reference and labels that library use as a deprecated-library migration concern. It does not, from that observation alone, establish a specific Joda-Time version, a vulnerable dependency graph, a runtime invocation, Android desugaring configuration, or a security impact.
known_false_positive_shapes: A comment, string literal, documentation snippet, or generated text contains org.joda.time syntax but no resolved Joda-Time symbol is used.
The matching code exists only in tests, benchmarks, samples, debug sources, or a build variant not shipped to users.
A transitive, compile-only, excluded, or dependency-substituted joda-time artifact is not packaged into the analyzed runtime artifact.
A same-named local type or wrapper causes lexical matching without binding to org.joda.time.
A formatter-like method call is present, but method resolution shows that it is not org.joda.time.format.DateTimeFormatter.
The dependency remains intentionally supported through a separate maintenance or vendor arrangement not represented by the detector's generic library classification.
A migration has already occurred on the executed path while stale Joda-Time references remain in unreachable or non-production code.
protocol: resolve joda-time dependency -> resolve Joda-Time symbol reference or formatter-factory call -> classify library use as a migration concern -> separately verify java.time/desugaring compatibility

detector_examples.message: joda-time library is deprecated. Migrate to java.time (Desugared).

source_audit.detail: none of the specification's findings mention org.joda.time.DateTime, org.joda.time.format.DateTimeFormat, org.joda.time.format.DateTimeFormatter
